thread.title: Tech Today: Zuck’s ‘Uneventful’ Day, Apple’s AI Ambition, Buying Tower Stocks

author: Tiernan Ray
title: Tech Today: Zuck’s ‘Uneventful’ Day, Apple’s AI Ambition, Buying Tower Stocks
text:
By Tiernan Ray Updated April 11, 2018 10:11 a.m. ET Here are some things going on today in the world of tech :
’Senator, We Show Ads' Shares of Facebook ( FB ) have been up and down this morning, and are currently up 21 cents at $165.25, as the Street breathes a sigh of relief that nothing much of any great significance seems to have come out of the first day of CEO Mark Zuckerberg ’s testimony before congress .
“Zuckerberg’s five hours of testimony yesterday was sometimes tedious, other times repetitive, but mostly — and this is a good thing — uneventful,” is how Evercore ISI’s Anthony DiClemente sums up the proceedings, as he reiterates an Outperform rating, and a $200 price target.
SunTrust’s Youssef Squali reiterates a Buy rating, and a $225 price target, writing that “Zuckerberg was able to keep his cool.” Squali actually thinks this is a “seminal event” that will “likely lead to increased regulation,” but he thinks such increased regulation “should still favor larger platforms like Facebook and Google at the end."
For a different view on the significance of the meetings, see my colleague Jonathan Swartz ’s write up .
Buy Tower Stocks on T-Mo, Sprint Noise The Street is parsing yesterday’s speculation Sprint ( S ) and T-Mobile US ( TMUS ) are back in merger talks.
Sprint stock is down 11 cents at $5.91, after soaring 17% yesterday. T-Mobile shares are up 17 cents at $63.30.
Craig Moffett ,of the eponymous Moffett Nathanson research house, asks “why now?” given the two broke off talks back in November.
He comes up with four reasons: just 2.5 years from a potentially Democratic administration that would be less merger-friendly, the upcoming quiet period in November for the next FCC auction, which would block merger talks, Sprint’s intent to spend more on its network, which would be a waste if T-Mobile hopes to own them.
And fourth, “the simple reality that Sprint doesn’t appear to have a path to sustainability."
SunTrust Robinson Humphrey ’s Greg Miller urges investors to buy the stocks of the tower companies, American Tower ( AMT ), Crown Castle International ( CCI ), and SBA Communications ( SBAC ).
“Ultimately, we see the prospects of a deal consummating as low as — if not lower than — last year’s aborted attempt,” writes Miller. “As such we believe weakness in tower stocks creates a buying opportunity."
Shares of all three tower names are rising today.
Apple’s AI Ambition Robert Cihra with Guggenheim this morning relates that he’s been digging into Apple ’s ( AAPL ) hiring of Alphabet ( GOOGL ) executive John Giannandrea , an expert in things such as machine learning.
Writes Cihra, “We have confirmed that Mr. Giannandrea will start later this month and report DIRECTLY to Apple’s CEO Tim Cook , which we consider critical so that he is not beholden to any one product or service.”
Cihra sees the appointment of Giannandrea as being initially about improving the “ Siri ” voice assistant, but more broadly, “a major move to redouble its position among the leading developers of Machine Learning."
Apple shares this morning are down 91 cents, or half a percent, at $172.34.
Intel’s Data Center Looks Strong Shares of Intel ( INTC ) are down 17 cents, at $51.11 after Macquarie Research ’s Srini Pajjuri this morning reiterated an Outperform rating on the shares, and a $58 price target, after concluding the company’s server chip sales are looking better than expected.
Conversations with people in the supply chain suggest " better than expected server builds ,” he writes, with Q1 server shipments "ahead of plan” at original design manufacturers, or ODMs, who make the vast majority of the world’s server computers, writes Pajjuri. He sees that strength in server shipments “accelerating into 2Q."
Pajjuri thinks Intel’s data center business could see revenue rise by 12% this year versus what Intel management had been forecasting as merely “high single digit growth."
Synaptics Gets an iPhone Reprieve Shares of sensor maker Synaptics ( SYNA ) are up $2.80, or 6.5%, at $46.81, after Vijay Rakesh with Mizuho this morning raised his rating on the shares to Buy from Neutral after concluding there will be a lot more of Apple’s new iPhones this fall that use the older LCD display technology, rather than OLED . That could be a “ tailwind ” for Synaptics, he thinks, given LCD models will contain Synaptics chips, the OLED models, not.
“While LCD was supposed to become obsolete with OLED,” he writes, but prices of OLED screens are still four to five times as expensive as LCD. Hence, “We believe the second half of 2018 could see LCD iPhones at 60% of the mix versus ~30-50% of new iPhones in 2H17.”
Rakesh hiked his price target on Synaptics to $55 from $42.
